segments.text: Did you know the busiest sites on the
internet ship new code in the middle of
the day, right through peak traffic, and
you never notice a thing?
No down for maintenance page, no late
night deploy window.
So, how do they replace a live app while
thousands of people are using it without
a single error?
It's called a blue/green deployment. And
by the end, you'll know exactly how to
build it on AWS.
We'll walk through each piece, and
there's a free hands-on lab to try it
yourself.
Here's how it works.
Start with the network.
Everything lives inside one Amazon VPC.
Our own private slice of AWS with an
internet gateway as the door to the
outside world.
But we don't put it all in one place.
Why?
Because data centers fail.
A power cut in one building shouldn't
take the whole app down.
So, we span the VPC across two
availability zones, two separate data
centers miles apart, and drop a public
subnet in each.
Lose a zone, the app keeps serving.
Inside, we run the app on an Amazon EC2
instance, version one.
Call it the blue server. It's what your
users hit today.
But you can't safely swap the code on a
server while people are using it.
So, we stand up a second identical EC2,
the green server running version two.
Two versions side by side.
Blue is live, green is waiting.
A server open to the whole internet gets
attacked.
So, we wrap both in one security group,
a firewall with a single rule.
Allow web traffic on port 80, block the
rest.
One rule, both servers covered.
Now, how does traffic find the right
server?
Not by pointing at machines. Servers
come and go.
So, we put each one in its own target
group.
TG blue and TG green.
Two labeled lanes.
The router talks to a lane, never a
machine.
That router is an application load
balancer.
One public front door spread across both
subnets, so it never has a single point
of failure.
It health checks every server and drops
any that stop responding.
Its listener rule is dead simple to
start.
100% to TG blue.
Everyone's on version one.
Green sits there, tested, dark.
Here's the payoff.
Flip everyone to green at once and one
hidden bug takes the whole site down.
So, we don't flip. We turn a dial.
Shift the listener weights.
80% blue, 20 green.
One in five users is on version two. And
we watch.
Something's wrong?
Back to 100 blue. Nobody noticed.
All clear?
Zero blue, 100 green.
The new version is live and no one ever
saw a maintenance page.
That's the whole setup.
A VPC across two zones for resilience.
Two EC2 servers for blue and green.
A security group to lock them down.
Target groups to sort them.
And a load balancer to move traffic on a
dial.
Every piece earns its place.
Together,
zero downtime deploys.
Now, knowing how it works is one thing.
Wiring it up yourself is where it
clicks. So, let's get your hands on it.
You'll get two kinds of free hands-on
labs.
First, a lab for each core piece, the
VPC, the EC2 servers, and the load
balancer.
So, you can practice the building blocks
on their own.
Then, a capstone where you wire the
whole blue/green setup together from
scratch.
In the capstone, you'll start with the
network, a VPC and public subnets across
two zones.
You'll launch two EC2 servers, blue on
version one and green on version two,
behind one security group.
You'll create TG blue and TG green and
register each server.
You'll stand up the load balancer, point
it at blue, then run the canary shift
yourself, 80/20, then full cutover to
green,
and watch the traffic move with zero
downtime.
By the end, you'll have shipped a new
version of a live app without dropping a
single request.
